q.s: The earliest evidence of a ploughed field, showing criss-cross furrows, comes from which pre-Harappan site?

q.x: Two crops sown in furrows at right angles indicate mixed cropping.

q.x: Late Harappan is 1900–1300 BCE; 2600–1900 BCE is the Mature phase.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Harappan craft centres is correct?

Chanhudaro had a bead-making factory with a furnace
Chanhudaro had the largest citadel in the Indus region

Rabatak – Two Ashvamedhas of Pushyamitra Shunga

q.s: The Boghazkoi inscription, which invokes Vedic gods like Indra, Mitra and Varuna, was found in:

q.x: Kautilya lists nine kinds of dasas, though Megasthenes reported no slaves in India.

q.x: Megasthenes in Indica stated that there were no slaves in India.

q.s: The oldest stupa in Andhra Pradesh is at:

The oldest stupa of Andhra is at Nagarjunakonda
The Amaravati stupa stands on the right bank of the Krishna
The Bhattiprolu stupa is in Rayalaseema

q.s: The Nalanda Mahavihara was founded by which Gupta ruler?

q.x: The Bagh caves are in Dhar district; their nine viharas are Buddhist.

q.s: The Second Battle of Panipat was fought in:

q.s: The main reason the Rajput states could not put up a combined opposition to the Turks was:
o: Constant feuds among the Rajput states
q.x: Mutual rivalries among Rajput states prevented a united front against the Turks.

q.s: What weight did population carry in Finance Commission devolution formulas, as mentioned in discussions of population growth?
q.x: Population has had a weight of about 15–25% in Finance Commission formulas.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Census 2011 is correct?
o: It was the 15th Census of India
q.x: Census 2011 was the 15th; growth was 17.7%; 68.9% was rural; Nagaland recorded negative growth.

q.s: Which State recorded negative population growth during 2001–11?
q.x: Nagaland recorded negative growth; Meghalaya the highest growth.

q.s: Among the Khasi of Meghalaya, property is inherited by the:
q.x: Khasi follow ultimogeniture: the youngest daughter (khadduh) inherits.

q.s: Who is regarded as a pioneer of family studies in India and wrote 'Marriage and Family in India'?
q.x: K.M. Kapadia pioneered family studies; A.M. Shah wrote The Household Dimension of the Family in India.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Self-respect marriages were validated by Section 7-A of the Hindu Marriage Act through a Tamil Nadu amendment
The Supreme Court read same-sex marriage into the Special Marriage Act in 2023
Live-in relationships are protected under Article 19
Self-respect marriages were started by B.R. Ambedkar
q.x: Periyar's self-respect marriages were validated in 1967; Supriyo (2023) declined same-sex marriage; live-in relations are protected under Article 21.

q.s: In the Supriyo case (October 2023), the Supreme Court:
o: Struck down the Special Marriage Act
Declined to read same-sex marriage into the Special Marriage Act
q.x: The Court left the question of legalising same-sex marriage to Parliament.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Caste and casteism mean the same thing
Casteism is a hereditary, endogamous group
Caste is only a political attitude
Caste is a social institution, while casteism is an attitude of partisan loyalty to one's own caste
q.x: Caste is a structure (hereditary, endogamous group); casteism is an attitude that uses caste for partisan gain.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The Self-Respect Movement (1925) was started by Periyar.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Fundamentalism cannot exist without inter-group conflict
Group exclusiveness is a cause of fundamentalism
Communalism and fundamentalism are the same thing
Fundamentalism is mainly doctrinal, while communalism is political mobilisation of religious identity
q.x: Fundamentalism is doctrinal; communalism is political. Group exclusiveness is a feature, not a cause, and fundamentalism can exist without inter-group conflict.

q.s: Under the pre-2022 employment zones of Andhra Pradesh, Zone IV comprised the districts of:
q.x: Zone IV was Rayalaseema; Zone I North Andhra; Zone II Godavari–Krishna; Zone III Guntur–Prakasam–Nellore.

q.s: Which of the following statements about maternity benefit in India is correct?
o: An adopting mother gets no maternity leave
From the third child, leave is 26 weeks
A woman with fewer than two children gets 26 weeks of maternity leave
q.x: 26 weeks for the first two children; 12 weeks from the third; adopting and commissioning mothers get 12 weeks.

q.s: The original Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 provided maternity leave of:
q.x: The 1961 Act gave 12 weeks.

q.s: Which of the following women-related laws is NOT correctly matched with its year?
o: Prohibition of Child Marriage Act in force – 2017
q.x: The Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 came into force on 1 November 2007.

q.s: The Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act was originally enacted in 1956 under the name:
q.x: It was the Suppression of Immoral Traffic in Women and Girls Act (SITA), renamed in 1986.

q.s: India's first all-women police station was set up in 1973 at:
q.x: The first all-women police station was opened at Kozhikode, Kerala, in 1973.

q.s: The Home Ministry has advised that women should form what share of the police force?
q.x: The advisory target is 33%; actual share is only about 11.7%.

q.s: Who defined public policy as 'whatever governments choose to do or not to do'?
q.x: Thomas Dye; Easton called it the 'authoritative allocation of values'.

q.s: Who is regarded as the founder of the policy sciences?
q.x: Harold Lasswell founded the policy sciences approach.

q.s: In Theodore Lowi's typology, land reforms and progressive income tax are examples of:
q.x: Redistributive policies transfer resources between groups.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched with Lowi's policy types?
q.x: Licensing and food-safety standards are regulatory policies.

q.s: The systems model of public policy, viewing policy as the output of the political system, was given by:
q.x: Easton's input–output model of the political system.

q.s: The Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY, 1999) merged IRDP, TRYSEM and:
q.x: SGSY merged IRDP, TRYSEM, DWCRA and allied schemes.

q.s: The credit-linked subsidy under PMEGP is routed through:
q.x: KVIC is the nodal agency for PMEGP.

q.s: Pre-school non-formal education under ICDS is meant for children in the age group of:
q.x: Pre-school education at Anganwadis is for 3–6 year olds.

q.s: Under ICDS, which of the following services is delivered through the health system (NHM) rather than the Anganwadi worker alone?
q.x: Immunisation, health check-ups and referrals come through the health system; nutrition and pre-school education through the Anganwadi Centre.

q.s: Under PM CARES for Children, COVID-19 orphans receive a corpus of ₹10 lakh at the age of:
q.x: Monthly stipend from 18, and the ₹10 lakh corpus at 23.

q.s: The Juvenile Justice (Amendment) Act, 2021 made which authority the focal point for adoption?
o: State Commission for Protection of Child Rights
q.x: Adoption orders are now passed by the District Magistrate.

q.s: The e-Shram portal for unorganised workers was launched by the Ministry of Labour in:
q.x: Launched on 26 August 2021.

q.s: Which of the following persons can register on the e-Shram portal?
o: An unorganised worker aged 16–59 who does not pay income tax
q.x: e-Shram is for unorganised workers aged 16–59 who are not income-tax payers or EPFO/ESIC members.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a contributory social insurance scheme?
q.x: NSAP is non-contributory social assistance; EPF, ESI and APY are contributory.

q.s: Under ILO Convention No. 102 (1952), a ratifying state must accept at least how many of the nine branches of social security?
q.x: At least three of the nine branches, including at least one specified branch.

q.s: 'Dulhan' scheme of Andhra Pradesh provides marriage assistance to:
q.x: Dulhan (2015) gave ₹50,000 to poor Muslim brides; Giri Puthrika was for tribal girls.

q.s: Annadata Sukhibhava, the successor of YSR Rythu Bharosa, gives farmers how much per year (including PM-KISAN)?
q.x: ₹20,000 a year: ₹14,000 from the State plus ₹6,000 from PM-KISAN.

q.s: Which community was notified as the sixth national minority in India in 2014?
q.x: Jains were notified in January 2014; the first five (Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis) in 1993.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a notified minority community at the national level in India?
q.x: Jews are not a notified national minority.

q.s: Which of the following Articles is NOT correctly matched with its provision?
o: Article 350 – Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities
Article 347 – Recognition of a language spoken by a substantial part of a State
Article 350A – Mother-tongue instruction at the primary stage
Article 350B – Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities
q.x: Article 350 deals with representation for redress of grievances in any language used in the Union or State.

q.s: 'Divya Kala Shakti' is an initiative related to persons with disabilities that:
q.x: Divya Kala Shakti is a cultural showcase; EKAM Fest promotes entrepreneurship.

q.s: Chabahar port, developed with Indian help to reach Afghanistan and Central Asia bypassing Pakistan, is located in:
q.x: Chabahar is in Iran's Sistan-Baluchestan, on the Gulf of Oman; it links to the INSTC.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Chabahar port is correct?
o: It is on the Caspian Sea
It is part of China's Belt and Road Initiative
It gives India access to Afghanistan and Central Asia without depending on Pakistan
q.x: Chabahar in Iran, on the Gulf of Oman, is linked to the INSTC and bypasses Pakistan.

q.s: Which of the following days is NOT correctly matched with its date?
q.x: World Environment Day is 5 June.

q.s: The WTO Appellate Body crisis since 2019 arises from:
o: The USA blocking appointments of members
q.x: The USA has blocked appointments, leaving the Appellate Body non-functional since December 2019.

q.s: The WTO dispute over India's solar-panel domestic-content requirement was brought by:
q.x: The USA brought the solar case; it also brought the export-subsidy (MEIS, SEZ) dispute.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the WTO is correct?
o: The General Council meets once in five years
The Trade Policy Review Body settles disputes
The Ministerial Conference is its highest body and meets at least once every two years
The Council for Trade in Goods oversees TRIPS
q.x: The General Council runs the WTO between Ministerial Conferences; the TPRB reviews trade policies; the Goods Council oversees GATT.

q.s: Which of the following BIMSTEC centres/events is NOT correctly matched with its location?
o: Centre for Weather and Climate – Bengaluru
q.x: The BIMSTEC Centre for Weather and Climate is at Noida.

q.s: The voting age in India was reduced from 21 to 18 years by the:
q.x: The 61st Amendment (1988, effective 1989) lowered the voting age.

q.s: Provincial autonomy was introduced in India by the:
q.x: The 1935 Act ended provincial dyarchy and gave responsible ministries from 1937, though Governors kept special powers.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a feature of the Government of India Act, 1935?
q.x: The 1935 Act ended provincial dyarchy (introduced in 1919) and provided for dyarchy at the Centre.

q.s: Child labour in hazardous work was dealt with by the Supreme Court in:
o: Bandhua Mukti Morcha v. Union of India
M.C. Mehta v. State of Tamil Nadu (1996)
q.x: M.C. Mehta (1996) directed a Child Labour Rehabilitation Welfare Fund.

q.s: Which of the following Directive Principles protects children against exploitation?
q.x: Articles 39(e) and 39(f) protect children; Art. 44 is the Uniform Civil Code, 48A environment, 50 separation of judiciary.

q.s: Since 2025, 25 June is observed in India as:
q.x: 25 June, the day the 1975 Emergency was declared, is observed as Samvidhan Hatya Diwas; Samvidhan Divas is 26 November.

q.s: The Twenty Point Programme was launched in 1975 by:
q.x: Indira Gandhi launched it during the Emergency; MoSPI monitors it.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT mentioned in the Preamble to the Constitution of India?
q.x: The Preamble mentions liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship; 'conscience' appears in Article 25.

q.s: Which of the following features of the Preamble is NOT correctly matched with its source?
o: Liberty, equality and fraternity – French Revolution
Justice – social, economic and political – French Revolution
q.x: The ideal of social, economic and political justice was taken from the Russian Revolution (1917).

q.s: Which of the following Articles is NOT correctly matched?
o: Article 16 – Equality of opportunity in public employment
q.x: Article 23 prohibits traffic in human beings and forced labour.

q.s: Which of the following Fundamental Rights is available to citizens only?
q.x: Articles 15, 16, 19, 29 and 30 are for citizens only; Articles 14, 21 and 25 cover all persons.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched with its new provision?
q.x: Criminal defamation is in Section 356 BNS.

q.s: How many grounds of reasonable restriction on freedom of speech and expression are listed in Article 19(2)?
q.x: Eight grounds, held to be exhaustive in Kaushal Kishor (2023).

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a ground of reasonable restriction under Article 19(2)?
q.x: Sedition is not listed in Article 19(2); the eight grounds include public order, defamation and sovereignty.

q.s: The right to establish and administer educational institutions under Article 30 belongs to:
q.x: Article 30(1) covers religious and linguistic minorities.

q.s: Public Interest Litigation (PIL) in India relaxes which traditional rule?
q.x: PIL lets public-spirited persons approach courts for others; the concept came from the USA.

q.s: Which case is regarded as a landmark in the development of PIL in India?
o: S.P. Gupta v. Union of India (1981)
q.x: S.P. Gupta (Judges' Transfer case, 1981) liberalised locus standi.

q.s: In Andhra Pradesh, the BC-E group (socially and educationally backward Muslims) has a reservation of:
q.x: BC-E has 4%; the total BC-A to BC-E share is 29%.

q.s: The first Backward Classes Commission of Andhra Pradesh, which reported in 1970, was the:
q.x: The Anantharaman Commission reported in 1970.

q.s: Which Article of the Constitution defines a Money Bill?
q.x: Article 110 defines Money Bills; Art. 110(2) excludes Bills only on fines, fees or local taxes.

q.s: Which of the following does NOT by itself make a Bill a Money Bill under Article 110?
o: Imposition or abolition of a tax
Regulation of borrowing by the Government of India
Custody of the Consolidated Fund of India
q.x: Under Article 110(2), fines, penalties, fees for licences or local taxes do not make a Bill a Money Bill.

q.s: A joint sitting of the two Houses of Parliament can NOT be held for which of the following?
o: Bill rejected by the Rajya Sabha
q.x: Joint sittings (Article 108) are not available for Money Bills and Constitution Amendment Bills.

q.s: Andhra State was formed on 1 October 1953 after the death of Potti Sriramulu following a fast of:
q.x: Potti Sriramulu died on 15 December 1952 after a 56-day fast.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 is correct?
o: It retained Part A, B and C States
It came into force on 1 November 1956 and ended the Part A, B, C classification
q.x: With the 7th Amendment it created 14 States and 6 UTs; Andhra State had been formed in 1953.

q.s: Which of the following Lok Sabha constituency extremes is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Lakshadweep is the smallest by electors; Malkajgiri is the largest.

q.s: Which of the following statements about parliamentary questions is correct?
o: Supplementary questions are allowed on unstarred questions
At most 30 starred questions are listed a day
A starred question is answered orally and allows supplementary questions
A short-notice question needs at least 10 days' notice
q.x: Starred questions are answered orally; at most 20 are listed a day; short-notice questions need less than 10 days' notice.

q.s: Since 2017, the Andhra Pradesh Legislature has met in an interim building at:
q.x: The interim Assembly building is at Velagapudi in Amaravati.

q.s: Which type of veto is NOT available to the President of India?
q.x: The qualified veto, overridable by a higher majority, belongs to the US President.

q.s: The President of India's pocket veto is possible because the Constitution:
o: Allows him to return Money Bills
Fixes no time limit for assent to Bills
Requires a two-thirds majority to override him
Permits him to dissolve the Rajya Sabha
q.x: No constitutional time limit is fixed for the President to act on ordinary Bills.

q.s: Repeated re-promulgation of ordinances was held to be a 'fraud on the Constitution' in:
o: D.C. Wadhwa v. State of Bihar (1987)
q.x: D.C. Wadhwa (1987); Krishna Kumar Singh (2017) reaffirmed it and held laying mandatory.

q.s: A presidential ordinance lapses if not approved within:
o: Six weeks of the reassembly of Parliament
Three months of the reassembly of Parliament
q.x: Article 123(2): it ceases six weeks after Parliament reassembles.

q.s: The electoral college for the election of the Vice-President of India consists of:
o: All members of both Houses of Parliament
Elected members of both Houses of Parliament and State Assemblies
Elected members of the Lok Sabha only
Members of the Rajya Sabha only
q.x: Both elected and nominated MPs vote; MLAs do not.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Vice-President of India is correct?
o: MLAs are part of his electoral college
He resigns by writing to the Speaker
A candidate must be qualified for election as a member of the Rajya Sabha
q.x: VP candidates must be qualified for the Rajya Sabha and need 20 proposers and 20 seconders; the electoral college is only MPs.

q.s: The Advocate General of a State is appointed under:
q.x: Article 165; the Attorney General is under Article 76.

q.s: The Advocate General of a State must be qualified to be appointed a judge of:
q.x: He must be qualified for appointment as a High Court judge; he holds office at the Governor's pleasure.

q.s: In Sita Soren v. Union of India (2024), the Supreme Court overruled which judgment on legislators' immunity for bribery?
q.x: A seven-judge Bench held there is no immunity for bribery connected with a speech or vote.

q.s: Which of the following Articles is NOT correctly matched?
o: Article 105 – Powers and privileges of Parliament
Article 122 – Courts not to inquire into proceedings of Parliament
Article 194 – Powers and privileges of Parliament
Article 212 – Courts not to inquire into proceedings of State Legislatures
q.x: Article 194 deals with privileges of State Legislatures.

q.s: Under Article 75(3), the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to:
q.x: Collective responsibility is to the Lok Sabha only.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Union Council of Ministers is correct?
o: It is collectively responsible to both Houses
The advice of the Council of Ministers is binding on the President under Article 74(1)
A non-member can never be a Minister
Ministers are individually responsible to the Lok Sabha Speaker
q.x: Article 74(1) makes the advice binding; collective responsibility is to the Lok Sabha; a non-member may be a Minister for six months.

q.s: Which case held that judicial review under Articles 226/227 and 32 is part of the basic structure, and tribunals cannot exclude High Courts?
q.x: L. Chandra Kumar (1997); Sampath Kumar (1987) had treated tribunals as a substitute for High Courts.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the UPSC is correct?
o: Its advice is binding on the government
Its advice is only advisory and not binding on the government
Action taken without consulting it is invalid
Selection by the UPSC gives a right to the post
q.x: UPSC's advice is advisory; non-consultation does not invalidate action; selection confers no right to appointment.

q.s: The salary and administrative expenses of the office of the CAG are:
o: Voted annually by the Lok Sabha
Charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
Fixed by the President each year
q.x: Charged expenditure protects the CAG's independence; his salary equals a Supreme Court judge's.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the CAG of India is NOT correct?
o: His administrative expenses are voted annually by the Lok Sabha
His salary equals that of a Supreme Court judge
He is not eligible for further office after retirement
He is appointed by the President
q.x: The CAG's expenses, including staff pensions, are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

q.s: 'Prisons and persons detained therein' is a subject in the:
q.x: It is Entry 4 of the State List; the Model Prisons Act, 2023 is only a guide for States.

q.s: The Sarkaria Commission on Centre-State relations was appointed in 1983 by the:
q.x: The Centre appointed it; Tamil Nadu had set up the Rajamannar Committee (1969).

q.s: Which of the following committees/commissions on Centre–State relations was appointed by a State government?
q.x: Tamil Nadu set up the Rajamannar Committee (1969); Sarkaria (1983) and Punchhi (2007) were appointed by the Centre.

q.s: A registered-unrecognised political party is delisted if it does not contest any election for:
q.x: RUPPs must contest an election at least once in six years; they must also report donations above Rs 20,000.

q.s: The Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968 was issued by the:
q.x: It is a statutory order of the ECI under the RPA 1951 and Article 324, not an Act of Parliament.

q.s: The Supreme Court held that the Election Commission cannot deregister a party merely for poor electoral performance in:
o: INC v. Institute of Social Welfare (2002)
q.x: Deregistration is possible only for fraud, ceasing allegiance to the Constitution or being declared unlawful.

q.s: Electronic Voting Machines were first used in India in 1982 at:
q.x: Parur, Kerala, 1982.

q.s: The VVPAT was first used in India in the 2013 bye-election to the Noksen constituency of:
q.x: Noksen (Nagaland), 2013.

q.s: The Marthandam rural reconstruction project in Travancore was run by:
q.x: Spencer Hatch ran it under the YMCA; Brayne ran the Gurgaon experiment, Mayer the Etawah project.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a component of the five-fold development aimed at by the Marthandam project?
q.x: It covered spiritual, mental, physical, economic and social development.

q.s: The PESA Act, extending Panchayati Raj to Fifth Schedule Areas, was passed in:
q.x: The Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996.

q.s: Which of the following statements about urban local bodies in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: Municipalities are graded on the basis of annual income
Municipalities are graded on the basis of population
Nagar Panchayats are constituted under Article 243B
There is no BC reservation in urban local bodies
q.x: AP grades municipalities by annual income; Nagar Panchayats are under Article 243Q; BCs get 33.33%.

q.s: A Nagar Panchayat for a transitional area is constituted under which Article?
q.x: Article 243Q provides Nagar Panchayats, Municipal Councils and Corporations.

q.s: Which of the following Articles inserted by the 106th Amendment is NOT correctly matched?
o: Article 330A – Women's reservation in the Lok Sabha
Article 239AA(2)(ba) – Women's reservation in the Delhi Assembly
Article 332A – Women's reservation in the Lok Sabha
q.x: Article 332A provides women's reservation in State Assemblies.

q.s: Which of the following tribal revolts is NOT correctly matched with its leader?
q.x: The Santhal Hul (1855–56) was led by Sidhu and Kanhu.

q.s: Which State pioneered State-wide social audits of MGNREGA works?
q.x: Andhra Pradesh, through SSAAT (2009).

q.s: Which State passed the first law making social audit of government programmes mandatory (2017)?
q.x: Meghalaya's Community Participation and Public Services Social Audit Act, 2017.

q.s: The Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act was passed in:
q.x: 2007; it makes maintenance a legal duty of children and relatives.

q.s: The National Policy on Older Persons was announced in:
q.x: NPOP 1999 listed 14 areas of intervention.

q.s: According to Census 2011, what share of India's urban population lived in million-plus cities?
The most important own source of revenue of urban local bodies in India is:
q.x: Property tax is the main own revenue of ULBs.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a function listed in the Twelfth Schedule for municipalities?
q.x: The Twelfth Schedule lists 18 functions; police is not one of them.

q.s: The Jawahar Rozgar Yojana (1989) was formed by merging:
q.x: JRY merged NREP and RLEGP.

q.s: SITRA (Supply of Improved Toolkits to Rural Artisans) was a sub-scheme of:
q.x: SITRA was under IRDP.

q.s: Which of the following PMGSY phases is NOT correctly matched with its focus?
o: PMGSY-III – Through routes and major rural links
q.x: PMGSY-I (2000) built new roads; PMGSY-II (2013) upgraded them.

q.s: Beneficiaries under PMAY-Gramin are identified from:
o: SECC 2011 data, verified by the Gram Sabha
q.x: SECC 2011 data are verified by Gram Sabhas.

q.s: Under PMAY-Gramin, the unit assistance for houses in plain areas is:
q.x: ₹1.20 lakh in plains; ₹1.30 lakh in hilly and difficult areas.

q.s: India's score of 25.8 in the Global Hunger Index 2025 places it in which category?
q.x: India ranked 102nd of 123 in the 'serious' category.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT an indicator of the Global Hunger Index?
q.x: The four GHI indicators are undernourishment, child stunting, child wasting and child mortality.

q.s: Which of the following statements about economic development is correct?
o: A large share of GDP from the primary sector indicates development
Structural transformation means a shift of activity from agriculture to industry and services
The Kerala model shows high human development needs high per capita income
A falling share of manufactured exports indicates development
q.x: A large primary share signals underdevelopment; Kerala achieved high human development at modest income.

q.s: Which of the following 'Super Six' schemes of Andhra Pradesh is NOT correctly matched with its benefit?
o: Talliki Vandanam – Rs 15,000 per school child
Deepam-2 – Free bus travel for women
Stree Shakti – Free bus travel for women
q.x: Deepam-2 provides 3 free LPG cylinders a year.

q.s: Which of the following Five Year Plans exceeded its growth target?
q.x: The Eighth Plan (1992–97) achieved about 6.8% against a 5.6% target.

q.s: Which of the following Five Year Plans is NOT correctly matched with its objective?
o: Ninth Plan – Growth with social justice and equity
Seventh Plan – Food, work and productivity
Fifth Plan – Removal of poverty and self-reliance
q.x: Human resource development was the Eighth Plan's objective.

q.s: The State Bank of India was formed on 1 July 1955 on the recommendation of the:
o: Gorwala Committee (All India Rural Credit Survey)
q.x: The AIRCS (A.D. Gorwala) recommended converting the Imperial Bank into SBI.

q.s: How many banks were nationalised in the first round of bank nationalisation in 1969?
q.x: 14 banks with deposits of ₹50 crore and above in 1969; six more in 1980.

q.s: Which of the following statements about bank nationalisation is correct?
o: Fourteen banks with deposits of ₹50 crore and above were nationalised in 1969
SBI was among the banks nationalised in 1969
The 1980 round was under Morarji Desai
q.x: SBI was formed separately in 1955; six banks were nationalised in 1980 under Indira Gandhi.

q.s: 'Indradhanush' (August 2015) was a plan for the revival of:
q.x: Indradhanush was a seven-point plan for PSBs.

q.s: In the '4R' strategy for public sector banks, the four Rs are Recognition, Resolution, Recapitalisation and:
q.x: The 4Rs: Recognition, Resolution, Recapitalisation and Reforms.

q.s: Stagflation refers to a situation of:
o: High inflation with slow growth and high unemployment
q.x: Stagflation combines inflation and stagnation.

q.s: Which of the following statements about inflation measures is correct?
o: Headline inflation is more stable than core inflation
The Consumer Food Price Index has 5 sub-groups
Vegetables carry the highest weight in the CFPI
Core inflation excludes volatile food and fuel prices
q.x: Headline inflation is more volatile; the CFPI has 10 sub-groups, with cereals carrying the highest weight.

q.s: Which item carries the highest weight in the Consumer Food Price Index?
q.x: Cereals carry the highest weight among the CFPI's sub-groups.

q.s: Under the FRBM framework, new guarantees given by the Central Government are capped at what share of GDP a year?
q.x: The FRBM framework caps incremental Central guarantees at 0.5% of GDP a year.

q.s: In Budget 2021-22, FCI's borrowing for food subsidy from which fund was ended and brought on-budget?
q.x: FCI's NSSF loans were ended and food subsidy was fully budgeted in 2021-22.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Union of India v. Mohit Minerals (2022) is correct?
o: It held GST Council recommendations binding on legislatures
It described India as a flexible federation
It treated the GST Council as a statutory body
It located the simultaneous GST power in Article 279A
q.x: The Court held recommendations persuasive; the Council is constitutional (Art. 279A) and the power flows from Art. 246A.

q.s: The power of Parliament and State legislatures to make laws on GST simultaneously flows from:
q.x: Article 246A; Article 279A creates the GST Council.

q.s: Which law replaced FERA, converting foreign-exchange violations into civil offences?
q.x: FEMA (1999, in force 2000) is a civil law, unlike the criminal FERA.

q.s: The committee on Capital Account Convertibility (1997) and on Fuller Capital Account Convertibility (2006) was headed by:
q.x: Both Tarapore Committees dealt with capital account convertibility.

q.s: In which of the following sectors is FDI NOT permitted in India?
q.x: Chit funds, Nidhi companies, lottery and railway operations (with exceptions) are prohibited; railway infrastructure allows 100% automatic FDI.

q.s: Which of the following statements about India's cropping pattern is correct?
o: Wheat has the largest cropped area in India
Rice-wheat expansion happened without assured MSP procurement
Shifting rice area to pulses raises urea use
